newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen down on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen down on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares on Friday extended Thursday's fall and analysts said the stronger selling after price-fixing and at continuous trade signalled another fall on Monday as the market maintained a generally flat trend.
The market fell 1.8 percent on Friday to 16,669.1 points after having previously gained 3.6 percent this week.

"It's hard to say if there'll be one more fall or a few but we seem to be entering a phase where there are no big moves of the index in either direction," said Artur Kobos, a trader at ING Baring Securities in Warsaw.
The market is seen next week at 16,000 to 17,000 points.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 1.8 percent to 16,669.1 points and turnover fell 11.3 percent to 179.3 million zlotys ($57 million) on all three markets. Losers led gainers by 77 to eight with nine stocks flat.
Analysts said recent optimistic inflation and GDP forecasts were a good sign but that this year's several large primary offers could draw cash from listed shares in the short term.

They said the market seemed fairly valued at current levels though some said stocks were still a bit expensive after the surge earlier this year and that the bourse might soon fall below 16,000 points.
Analysts said Espebepe tumbled 9.6 percent after Thursday's news the largest creditor of the debt-ridden builder is against the debt-restructuring deal it proposed.

Analysts said paper firm Celuloza Swiecie could stay between 20 and 22 zlotys ($6.4-$7.0) after starting trade 4.9 percent above issue at 21.5 zlotys ($6.8), though bears saw falls for Poland's largest paper firm after its poor first-quarter earnings figures.
